summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic pancreatitis, and asthma was admitted for worsening epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back, nausea, and alcohol withdrawal symptoms. He had been drinking heavily and presented with tremors and hallucinations consistent with delirium tremens. His pain was attributed to an acute exacerbation of chronic pancreatitis, despite a normal lipase. He also had mild alcoholic hepatitis with elevated AST and bilirubin, and an asthma exacerbation requiring albuterol nebulizers and a steroid burst. He was managed with CIWA protocol for withdrawal, IV fluids, pain control with hydromorphone, and respiratory support. His condition improved over five days—he stabilized, tolerated a regular diet, and had resolution of withdrawal symptoms. He was discharged home with pain medication, continued liver and asthma therapies, and referrals for alcohol rehabilitation and follow-up care.
